implemented-requirements.description: Hub restore drill.

statements.description: The hub restore drill starts an old backup, returns clients to current checkpoints, and restores a nested view.
statements.remarks: Your organization chooses backup schedules and recovery.

implemented-requirements.description: Hub recovery exercise.

statements.description: The hub restore drill exercises recovery from a cold backup without retaining signing or encryption keys in that backup.
statements.remarks: Your organization approves and records recovery exercises.

implemented-requirements.description: On Kubernetes each hub runs hardened.

statements.description: When the site stack deploys hubs on Kubernetes, each hub is a StatefulSet of one replica that runs as user 65532 with a read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation, every capability dropped, the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile, no service account token and a memory limit; its health check is its liveness and readiness probe, its TLS, signing and encryption key files are mounted from Secrets with mode 0440, its volume is on the encrypted site class, and no autoscaler is rendered.
statements.remarks: Your organization lists the site's hubs in the site file and runs them on the site's cluster.

implemented-requirements.description: Each hub ends its own TLS and is not behind the shared ingress.

statements.description: When the site stack deploys hubs on Kubernetes, several hubs on one site each render as their own StatefulSet with their own volume, and no Ingress in the site stack routes to any hub. Sessions reach a hub at its cluster address and members at its node port, both plain TCP to the hub's own TLS on port 8443, and each hub's server certificate is issued by site-pki-hub for its site name and cluster names.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which projects each hub serves and which members may reach its node port.

control-implementations.description: Statements about the hub from the 44.1 coverage work (44.1-11).

implemented-requirements.description: The hub admits a device only as the project's signed roster says, and drops it when the roster revokes it.

statements.description: The hub follows each project's signed roster for who may connect. A device the roster does not have gets no session, and once the roster records device.revoke the device's token is refused and a new session is refused too. Only the staff lead's or deputy's device can register an invitation, and an invitation the roster records as used is refused. CI tests of the hub prove each of these, on the same hub code a self-hosted container and a Kubernetes site run.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who may lead a staff project, approves each person's admission, reviews the roster on its own schedule and removes people who leave.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub logs its events as JSON lines with an event name, redacted before they are written.

statements.description: The hub logs the events it handles (start and refused start, the join desk's outcomes, state directory changes, checkpoint conflicts) as one JSON line each, with time, level and event name first. A refused setting stops the hub with one hub.start_refused line naming the setting, never its value, and join desk lines carry only the project id, the invitation id and a reason word. CI tests of the hub's logger prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects the events it needs from each component, collects the hub's log lines, and decides how long it keeps them.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub detects and stops join secret guessing, a device that signs two entries at one place, and floods.

statements.description: The hub watches for misuse and stops it. After five join posts with a wrong MAC an invitation is locked; a device that signs two entries at one place is quarantined and its token refused; and calls past the per-address and per-writer rates are refused with Retry-After. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization collects the hub's log lines, watches them with its other monitoring, and responds to what they show.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub's configuration is a fixed set of HUB_ settings with safe defaults; anything else stops it.

statements.description: The hub's configuration is a fixed set of HUB_ settings. Without them it listens only on 127.0.0.1, port 8443, with the default state directory and no public address. An unknown HUB_ name, a relative state directory, a bad port, host or public address stops it, without the value being repeated. The hub has no runtime package dependencies. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization records the settings it runs each hub with as its baseline and reviews changes to them.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub refuses to start on a Node.js older than 26.13.1 and has no runtime package dependencies.

statements.description: The hub refuses to start on a Node.js release older than 26.13.1, naming the version it needs, and has no runtime package dependencies, so a fix to it arrives as a new hub release or a Node.js update. CI tests of the hub prove the version check and the empty dependency list.
statements.remarks: Your organization installs Node.js and hub updates within the time it sets for security fixes.

implemented-requirements.description: A revoked device loses its token and open stream at once.

statements.description: As soon as the roster records device.revoke, the hub refuses the device's token, refuses a new session, and closes the device's open event stream. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides when a person poses a risk and has the staff lead revoke their devices within the time it sets.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub sends each device only the cells it holds.

statements.description: The hub passes a project's entries only to devices that hold the cell they are in: a member sees only the streams and grant hashes of its cells, a member of one compartment receives no frame, page or blob of another, and a device not on a cell's access list cannot post presence to it. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which people are cleared for which compartments.

implemented-requirements.description: Only the lead's or deputy's device registers invitations and reads join requests; a hub device gets no session.

statements.description: On the hub only the staff lead's or deputy's device can register an invitation or list join requests; a member's device is refused 403. The hub's own device, admitted to hold the project, gets no person session. A member cannot write a roster entry such as member.invite. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who holds the lead and deputy roles.

implemented-requirements.description: A member's device cannot run the lead's functions on the hub.

statements.description: A member's device cannot register an invitation, list join requests or write a roster entry reserved for the lead and deputy: the hub refuses each. CI tests of the hub prove each refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who holds the lead and deputy roles.

implemented-requirements.description: A hub session token ends after 15 minutes.

statements.description: A hub session token works for 15 minutes and is then refused; the device opens a new session with a fresh signed answer. A device holds at most 8 tokens per project. CI tests of the hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets how long its people's editor sessions may stay signed in.

implemented-requirements.description: Devices reach the hub only over TLS 1.3.

statements.description: Devices reach the hub only over TLS 1.3: a client limited to TLS 1.2 fails the handshake and a plain HTTP client gets no answer. CI tests of the built hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides from which networks its people may reach the hub.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub limits rates, sizes and slow clients.

statements.description: The hub limits what one client can take: per-address rates for join, enrolment and session calls and per-writer rates for appends, each refused with Retry-After; size caps that refuse a body before it is read; and slow clients cut off after a short grace. CI tests of the hub prove each limit.
statements.remarks: Your organization protects the network in front of the hub and sizes the host it runs on.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub's own bookkeeping for rate limits has a fixed size.

statements.description: The hub's rate-limit buckets never pass their cap: a flood of addresses and writers keeps at most the set number of buckets, the least recently used idle bucket going first. CI tests of the hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization sizes the host the hub runs on.

implemented-requirements.description: Devices reach the hub only over TLS 1.3, and project content is sealed before it leaves the device.

statements.description: Devices reach the hub only over TLS 1.3, and what they send is sealed on the device before it travels: the content, labels and decision reasons of cells not granted to the hub are in no byte the hub sends or stores. CI tests of the hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization issues the hub's TLS certificate and decides from which networks its people may reach the hub.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub speaks only TLS 1.3.

statements.description: The hub speaks only TLS 1.3: a client limited to TLS 1.2 fails the handshake and a plain HTTP client gets no answer. CI tests of the built hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization issues the hub's TLS certificate.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub closes a connection that does not authenticate in time.

statements.description: The hub closes a connection that sends nothing before its deadline, and cuts off a client that stops in the middle of its headers after about 5 seconds. CI tests of the hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the network timeouts in front of the hub.

implemented-requirements.description: A hub token works only on the TLS connection it was issued on.

statements.description: A hub session is bound to its TLS connection: the answer that opens it is signed over that connection's keying material, and a token copied to another connection is refused there while it still works on its own. CI tests of the hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization protects its people's computers, which hold the device keys.

implemented-requirements.description: Each hub session starts from a fresh random challenge that works once.

statements.description: Each hub session starts from a challenge of 32 fresh random bytes, never stored or cached, and an answer that already opened a session cannot open another. CI tests of the hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization protects its people's computers, which hold the device keys.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub stores project content only as the devices sealed it.

statements.description: The hub stores and forwards project content only as the devices sealed it: no product name, title, text, label or decision reason of a cell not granted to the hub is in any byte of its state folder or its log, and a presence value is in no state file. CI tests of the hub prove each of these, with positive controls that find canaries where they are put.
statements.remarks: Your organization protects the host or volume the hub's state folder is on, and its backups.

implemented-requirements.description: Content of cells not granted to the hub stays encrypted at rest on the hub.

statements.description: Content of cells not granted to the hub stays encrypted on the hub: it arrives sealed, large products travel as sealed blobs, and none of their canaries is in any state folder byte. CI tests of the hub prove this, with a positive control.
statements.remarks: Your organization protects the host or volume the hub's state folder is on, and its backups.

implemented-requirements.description: Each hub log line carries the time, level and event, and its fields cannot overwrite them.

statements.description: Each hub log line carries the time, the level and the event name first, followed by the event's fields, and no field can overwrite the time, level or event. CI tests of the hub's logger prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which fields it needs in each record across the deployment.

implemented-requirements.description: Secrets, tokens and bodies never reach the hub's log.

statements.description: The hub redacts before a line reaches the log: registered secret values become [secret:NAME], and tokens, MACs, challenges, keying material, signatures, sealed values and bodies are dropped with their length kept. Only the logger writes to standard output. CI tests of the hub's logger prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization protects the place it collects the hub's log lines and decides who may read them.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub writes its events through one logger, as JSON lines.

statements.description: All of the hub's events go through one logger, which writes each as one JSON line; no other hub source writes to standard output or calls console methods. CI tests of the hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization collects the hub's standard output with its other records.

implemented-requirements.description: A device opens a hub session only by signing a fresh challenge over its own connection.

statements.description: A device opens a hub session only by signing a fresh 32-byte challenge, for this project and this hub, over the keying material of its own TLS connection, within 60 seconds. An answer with changed content, for another hub or project, an older or reused challenge, or another connection's keying material is refused. CI tests of the hub prove each refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which devices are admitted to each project.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub loads its keys only from files and never from plain environment values.

statements.description: The hub loads its TLS key and its own keys only from files: a key set as a plain environment value is refused, and every loaded value is registered with the log redactor so it never reaches a log line. As a self-hosted container, a key file open to group or others is refused as well. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization protects the host or Kubernetes secrets that hold the hub's key files and rotates them on its own schedule.

implemented-requirements.description: No hub key is embedded in the hub, its image or the repository.

statements.description: No hub key is built into the hub or its image. The hub refuses its secrets as plain environment values, git ignores the hub's secret files and database, and the image's build context lets in no secret or service state. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization generates each hub's keys at its site and keeps them out of its own images and repositories.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub refuses an entry, join request or blob that does not match its signature or hash.

statements.description: The hub checks what it is given before it keeps it: an entry signed by another key than its writer's is refused, a body whose size or hash differs from its header is refused, a join request whose signature does not verify is refused, and a blob whose bytes do not match its hash is refused. CI tests of the hub prove each refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization investigates a refusal the hub logs.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub refuses malformed, oversized and out-of-order input before it acts on it.

statements.description: The hub checks each input before it acts: a session call or enrolment that is not in the expected shape is refused as malformed, a header over 4 KiB is refused before it is read, and an entry beyond the next sequence of its writer's log is refused. CI tests of the hub prove each refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization investigates refusals the hub logs.

implemented-requirements.description: Hub errors name the problem without a token, key, value or path.

statements.description: The hub's errors say what went wrong without giving anything away: no error body holds the token, the challenge or the path, no enrolment refusal holds a value, a hash or a key, and a damaged hub build prints one fixed sentence with no path or stack. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who may read the hub's log lines.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub removes accepted join requests after 7 days and unreferenced uploads after 24 hours.

statements.description: The hub keeps an accepted join request for 7 days and then removes it from the list and the database, also at start after a long stop, and removes an uploaded blob that no entry referenced within 24 hours. CI tests of the hub prove each removal.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides how long project content is kept and removes projects it no longer needs.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub acknowledges an append only after it is committed, and keeps every acknowledged append through a crash.

statements.description: The hub answers an append only after its database commit, so an acknowledged append survives a crash: the built hub killed with SIGKILL after 20 acknowledged appends restarts on its state directory with all 20. CI tests of the hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization backs up the hub's state directory and tests its restore.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub opens no outbound connection and has no runtime package dependencies.

statements.description: The hub does only what it needs: while serving it opens no outbound connection, its health check connects only to its own loopback address, and it has no runtime package dependencies. CI tests of the hub prove each of these, with a scanner that is tested to report every network client form.
statements.remarks: Your organization restricts the hub's host and network to what the hub needs.
